description: Pins protocol::aead_seal_ctx + protocol::aead_open_ctx byte mapping (XChaCha20-Poly1305 + CTX commitment outer per Chan & Rogaway 2022) AND each of the 7 pub aad_* builder functions' canonical byte assembly. 12 cases: 7 aad_canonical_bytes (one per builder) + 2 encrypt (short empty-AAD + medium content-AAD plaintext) + 1 decrypt_ok (round-trip) + 2 decrypt_aead_fail (tag-tamper + AAD-tamper). Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_ctx_aead_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/aead.rs).

cases.description: Canonical bytes from aad_password_wrap with FAST_TEST KdfParams (m_kib=8, t=1, p=1, v=0x13). Pins the §5.2 password-wrap AAD assembly: 'myne.v0.1|' prefix + version byte + role 'pw' + serialized 11-byte KDF params block.
Canonical bytes from aad_recovery_wrap. Same FAST_TEST KdfParams; differs from aad_password_wrap only in the role byte ('rk' instead of 'pw' — drift detection across the password/recovery split).

Canonical bytes from aad_vault_items_key_wrap with items_key_id = 0xAB×16. Pins the singleton-itemsKey wrap AAD ('itemsKey' role with NO per-note UUID — distinguishes this builder from aad_note_item_key_wrap whose name differs by one trailing 's').

Canonical bytes from aad_note_item_key_wrap with items_key_id = 0xAB×16 + note_uuid = 0xCD×16. Pins the per-note item_key wrap AAD ('item-key' role WITH note_uuid). Visually adjacent to aad_vault_items_key_wrap; one-character difference in name pins a real type-confusion-class hazard (§5.2 spec note).

Canonical bytes from aad_note_content_encrypt. Same items_key_id + note_uuid pair; differs from aad_note_item_key_wrap in the role byte AND adds the hardcoded content_type 'text/markdown' (13 ASCII bytes with 2-byte BE length prefix). 58-byte total AAD per spec §5.2.

Canonical bytes from aad_prefs_blob with account_number_hash = 0x12×16. Pins the §9.5.3 39-byte vault.prefs AAD: 'myne.v0.1|' prefix (10) + version byte (1) + length-prefixed UTF-8 role 'prefs-blob' (2+10) + account_number_hash (16).

Canonical bytes from aad_search_index_blob with account_number_hash = 0x12×16 (MYND-29, §9.6). Pins the 46-byte vault.search AAD: 'myne.v0.1|' prefix (10) + version byte (1) + length-prefixed UTF-8 role 'search-index-blob' (2+17) + account_number_hash (16). Same shape as aad_prefs_blob but a distinct 17-byte role string — domain-separates the search index from the prefs blob. NOTE: the AAD role 'search-index-blob' is DISTINCT from the HKDF KEK role 'search-index-key' (hkdf-sha256 vectors); they are different load-bearing constants.

Encrypt 3-byte plaintext 'abc' with empty AAD. Primitive-level coverage of aead_seal_ctx without binding to any AAD builder — proves the CTX commitment outer construction works at the bare-bytes layer. Expected sealed = 3-byte ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag = 35 bytes.

Encrypt 256-byte plaintext (byte i = i mod 256) with AAD = aad_note_content_encrypt(items_key_id=0xAB×16, note_uuid=0xCD×16) (58-byte content-encrypt AAD). Realistic AEAD invocation matching the .myn-blob inner-content layer. Expected sealed = 256-byte ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag = 288 bytes.

Round-trip the sealed blob from encrypt-medium-content-aad back to the 256-byte plaintext under the same key + nonce + AAD. Proves aead_open_ctx recovers exactly the plaintext bytes that aead_seal_ctx consumed.

Last byte of the 32-byte CTX commitment tag flipped via XOR 0xFF. aead_open_ctx MUST surface Err(ProtocolError::AeadFailure) — the CTX commitment construction (SHA-256 over key||nonce||AAD-len||AAD||Poly1305-tag) catches the modification at the constant-time comparison step.
cases.informational_tamper_description: last byte of 32-byte CTX commitment tag region flipped via XOR 0xFF

cases.description: Sealed blob from encrypt-medium-content-aad with caller passing a DIFFERENT AAD (aad_prefs_blob bytes instead of aad_note_content_encrypt) to the verifier. aead_open_ctx MUST surface Err(ProtocolError::AeadFailure) — the CTX commitment includes the AAD bytes, so swapping AAD invalidates the tag. Same non-distinguishing variant as the tag-tamper case per spec §6.4.
cases.informational_tamper_description: AAD swap: caller passes aad_prefs_blob bytes instead of the aad_note_content_encrypt bytes the encoder used
